title: Check newly recovered key-pair material for direct authenticated DBX reuse
why: E347/E354/E355 establish real recovered key-pair objects, but expressly leave reuse open. Earlier codec trials preceded this source recovery. A finite direct-key authentication check against the physically observed 12-byte page reserve can distinguish actual reuse from labels alone without guessing passwords or publishing secrets. Failure will not exclude other KDFs or protocols.
proposition: A source-valid 32-byte secret from a recovered key pair directly authenticates captured DBX pages under a basic 8-byte-nonce/4-byte-tag trailer layout.
negation: These finite direct-key/layout combinations do not authenticate; other derivations and codecs remain unresolved.
